title: Extension of a supported perfect object from an affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ an affine open. Choose derived module categories [def-pc-derived-category] in one Hom universe on $X$, its localized open sites, $V$, and its localized open sites. Let $S\subseteq X$ be closed and contained in $V$. For every perfect quasi-coherent $B\in D(\mathcal O_V)$ [def-pc-perfect-complex] with all cohomology stalks outside $S$ zero, there exists a perfect quasi-coherent $A\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ with all cohomology stalks outside $S$ zero, such that for every $C\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and integer $n$, $\operatorname{Hom}(A[n],C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B[n],C|_V)$ as types. Here $C|_V$ is exact over-site restriction followed by the canonical module equivalence [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps]. The proof constructs $A$ by exact extension by zero; no detection property is asserted.

proof.text: Let E be the actual extension-by-zero presheaf followed by module sheafification on the localized site of V, and e the over equivalence. Construct L=e.inverse followed by E. Exactness and the adjunction E ⊣ restriction come from lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact. Compose with the equivalence adjunction. Apply the proved source-library mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction and rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory to obtain D(L) ⊣ D(restriction). The isomorphism E followed by restriction to identity from lem-pc-open-extension-restriction-iso, composed with e.counitIso, gives L followed by scheme restriction isomorphic to identity. Derive this isomorphism using mapDerivedCategoryCompIso, mapDerivedCategoryNatIso and mapDerivedCategoryIdIso. Hence the derived left adjoint is fully faithful and its unit is invertible.

source.place: Lemma 20.33.6 (2), together with Tags 08DP, 08D5, 00A7 (3)-(4) and the supported Koszul construction of Tag 0A9A

proof.text: The usual restriction/direct-image adjunction of module sheaves, transported through overFunctorEquiv, gives the right derived adjunction D(restriction) ⊣ Rj_*. Transpose the inverse of the unit of D(L) ⊣ D(restriction) to obtain phi:D(L)(B)→Rj_*B. Its adjunct composed with that unit is identity, so the canonical comparison clause of lem-pc-supported-open-pushforward makes phi invertible. The perfection clause makes Rj_*B perfect. The affine inclusion is quasi-compact because its source is compact and its target is quasi-separated, and it is separated as an open immersion. Apply lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh. Transport quasi-coherence degreewise and local strictly perfect representatives across phi to A=D(L)(B). The data of A is this explicit exact construction, rather than a witness chosen from an unproved mere existence result.

source.place: Lemma 20.33.6 (2), together with Tags 08DP, 08D5, 00A7 (3)-(4) and the supported Koszul construction of Tag 0A9A

proof.text: Exact L commutes with homology, so H^n(A) is isomorphic to L(H^n(B)). At a point inside V, use the previously constructed L followed by restriction isomorphism, overFunctorEquiv and restrictStalkNatIso to identify this stalk with the stalk of H^n(B). Outside S it is zero by the hypothesis. At a point outside V, apply lem-sc-module-extension-by-zero-stalk-maps-outside to the inverse-over-equivalence of H^n(B). Thus A is supported on S. This covers empty V and empty S without selecting points.

source.place: Lemma 20.33.6 (2), together with Tags 08DP, 08D5, 00A7 (3)-(4) and the supported Koszul construction of Tag 0A9A

proof.text: The canonical commShiftIso for D(L) identifies A[n] with D(L)(B[n]). Compose its Hom-congruence equivalence with the derived adjunction homEquiv at B[n] and arbitrary C. This proves the Hom formula without imposing support or quasi-coherence on C.

lean.statement: theorem supported_open_extension (X : Scheme.{u}) [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] [∀ U : X.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))] (V : X.affineOpens) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (V : X.Opens).toScheme.toRingedSpace))] [∀ U : (V : X.Opens).toScheme.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings (V : X.Opens).toScheme.toRingedSpace).over U))] (S : Set X) (hS : IsClosed S) (hSV : S ⊆ (V : X.Opens)) (B : schemeDerivedQCohCategory (V : X.Opens).toScheme) (hB : Scheme.IsPerfect (V : X.Opens).toScheme B.obj) (hsB : ∀ (n : ℤ) (x : (V : X.Opens).toScheme), x.val ∉ S → Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (V : X.Opens).toScheme.toRingedSpace)) n).obj B.obj).val.presheaf x))) : ∃ A : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X, Scheme.IsPerfect X A.obj ∧ (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∉ S → Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj A.obj).val.presheaf x))) ∧ ∀ (C : schemeDerivedCategory X) (n : ℤ), Nonempty ((A.obj⟦n⟧ ⟶ C) ≃ (B.obj⟦n⟧ ⟶ (schemeOpenRestriction X (V : X.Opens)).mapDerivedCategory.obj C))
